content.rationale:
The decision models the commit policy of a discard as Quint state, so the gate is a model-check in the house form: `specs/drafts/discard_commit_check.qnt` imports the record form, its two states and the registry variable from `draft_state` (tvtnokzu, `specs/drafts/state.qnt`), imports one action from the model at `specs/drafts/discard_commit.qnt`, and fixes the interface that model must carry: module `draft_discard_commit`, one action `discardCommit(handles: List[str], prepared: Set[str], failed: bool)` over the registry variable `records`, total over its three inputs. `prepared` is the check's abstraction of the per-draft change, workspace and directory work: a handle in it is a named draft whose three acts have all completed before the call decides. `failed` says whether any of those acts, or the removal itself while no record has yet left the store, failed before the commit point. The check imports only that action and reads no helper, type or variable the model defines; the model must not define the check's own `gate`-prefixed helpers (`gateNamed`, `gateAccepted`, `gateWithoutNamed`, `gateCommitReady`), because the TLA+ flattener merges the two modules' definitions and a shared name would shadow the check's condition.

The check seeds a registry the prerequisites admit: three open drafts (`h1`, `h2`, `h3`) over two nodes and two landed records (`h4`, `h5`), each filed under its own handle through the state module's own `filed` and `landed`. It records the registry and the three inputs of each call immediately before the call, then runs the model's action, so every invariant relates the registry after the call both to the registry before it and to the inputs that call was given. The call pool covers an empty call; one, two and three open records; a handle named twice; prepared handles the call does not name; a failure after every named draft is prepared; a failure while some named draft is unprepared; a call with no named draft prepared; a prepared landed record; an open record mixed with a landed one; an open record mixed with a handle the registry does not hold; two landed records; and an absent handle on its own. From any reachable registry the same pool is applied again, so commit traces, refusal traces and failure traces are all explored.

The invariants pin the policy from the three sides its prerequisites fix. `NoRemovalBeforeCommit` - a record leaves the store only when the call has reached its commit, so an unprepared named draft or a failure before the commit leaves the registry exactly as it was. `CommitIsExact` - a call that reaches the commit removes exactly the records it names, each of them open, and nothing else. `FailureLeavesRegistry` and `FailureLeavesNamedOpen` - a failure before the commit leaves every record at its handle and every named open draft still present, field for field. `OthersUntouched` - every record the call did not name stays at its handle and is not rewritten, renamed or moved, and so no record turns from `open` to `landed`. `LandedNeverRemoved` - a landed record is still there, unchanged, after any call. `NoRecordAdded` - the registry after a call holds a subset of what it held before, because a discard files no record. `WholeCallAtomic` - the registry after a call is either exactly the one before it or exactly the one before it without every named handle, so no per-handle partial removal exists. Fifteen runs execute one case each and assert its outcome: a commit of one open record, of two, with prepared extras not named, and with a handle named twice; a failure after all named drafts are prepared, on one handle and on two; no commit with one of two named drafts prepared; a failure while a named draft is unprepared; no named draft prepared; a prepared landed record refused whole; an open record mixed with a landed one refused whole; an open record mixed with an absent handle refused whole; two landed records refused whole; an empty call; and a failure whose named records stay open and are removed by a later invocation.

Each prerequisite is used for one thing. nwswzlnw fixes where the commit sits: the removal is last, a failure at any earlier point refuses the invocation, the refusal removes nothing, and no named record begins to leave while any named draft's work is still to run - `NoRemovalBeforeCommit`, `FailureLeavesRegistry`, `FailureLeavesNamedOpen` and `WholeCallAtomic` read those clauses over the model. qmpskomv fixes the selection and the removal: a call is accepted exactly when every named handle is an `open` record, an accepted call removes exactly the records it names, every other record stays at its handle, a landed record is never removed, and no record is added - `CommitIsExact`, `OthersUntouched`, `LandedNeverRemoved` and `NoRecordAdded`, together with the refusal runs. tvtnokzu fixes the record's form, its two states and the registry map the action steps; the check imports that module and restates none of it, so the record shape, the states and the content-identity base stay the state model's.

The check is run mechanically. `quint typecheck specs/drafts/discard_commit_check.qnt` checks the grammar and the types, including that the model really exposes the action with the three-input signature. `quint verify specs/drafts/discard_commit_check.qnt --main=draft_discard_commit_check --init=initCheck --backend=tlc --invariant=NoRemovalBeforeCommit,CommitIsExact,FailureLeavesRegistry,FailureLeavesNamedOpen,OthersUntouched,LandedNeverRemoved,NoRecordAdded,WholeCallAtomic --max-steps=6` runs the explicit-state checker over every trace to the bound. `quint test specs/drafts/discard_commit_check.qnt` executes the fifteen runs. The module starts from its seeded registry rather than from the state module's empty `init`, so the verifier is given `--init=initCheck`; TLC keeps the run free of the Apalache flattening step, and a JDK-backed `--backend=apalache` is the same check when a JDK is present.

The check tracks no wording of the decision. It fixes the action's contract - a call either removes exactly the open records it names after every named draft is prepared and no act failed, or leaves the registry unchanged - which is what the decision models, so a rewording that leaves that contract unchanged leaves the check intact. A failure that happens after a record has left the store is outside the model and outside the check, as nwswzlnw leaves the registry write's later behaviour to its own commitment; so are the order of the change, workspace and directory acts among themselves, the exact jj invocations, the refusal's wording, stream and exit status, and the store's serialization. The seeded handles, node ids, edits, workspaces and bases are values the check chooses, none of them derived from a prerequisite. The node states no verdict: whether a particular artifact satisfies the check is a finding about a run, not content of this evaluation.
